name: Gradient Computation and Back-Propagation
text:
# Gradient Computation and Back-Propagation

Also called: Differentiable Rendering Gradients, Backpropagation in 3DGS

## Overview
Gradient Computation and Back-Propagation defines the mathematical and algorithmic mechanisms for propagating loss gradients from rendered pixels back to the parameters of [3D Gaussian primitives](#12855-gaussian-representation-and-truncation.md) (position, scale, rotation, opacity, color) and camera intrinsics/extrinsics. It solves the problem of optimizing radiance fields by enabling end-to-end training via [automatic differentiation](#7151-automatic-differentiation-reverse-adjoint-mode.md) or custom analytical backward passes. It sets itself apart from sibling methods by focusing on the core differentiability of the rendering equation, whereas siblings like [Physical Parameter Optimization](4111-physical-parameter-optimization.md) or [WildGaussians](6064-wildgaussians.md) extend or modify this core gradient path for specific domains (e.g., ToF, semantic features, or dynamic scenes).

## Shared principles
The core principle is the application of the chain rule through the [differentiable volume rendering](#43-differentiable-volume-rendering.md) equation. For a pixel $\mathbf{x}$, the rendered color $\mathbf{C}(\mathbf{x})$ is computed via alpha [compositing](#2436-compositing.md):
$$
\mathbf{C}(\mathbf{x}) = \sum_{k=1}^{N} \mathbf{c}_k \alpha_k(\mathbf{x}) T_k(\mathbf{x})
$$
where $N$ is the number of Gaussians sorted by depth, $\mathbf{c}_k$ is the color, $\alpha_k(\mathbf{x})$ is the opacity, and $T_k(\mathbf{x}) = \prod_{j=1}^{k-1} (1 - \alpha_j(\mathbf{x}))$ is the transmittance.

The gradient of the loss $L$ with respect to a primitive parameter $\theta$ is:
$$
\frac{\partial L}{\partial \theta} = \sum_{\mathbf{x}} \frac{\partial L}{\partial \mathbf{C}(\mathbf{x})} \frac{\partial \mathbf{C}(\mathbf{x})}{\partial \theta}
$$
The term $\frac{\partial \mathbf{C}(\mathbf{x})}{\partial \theta}$ is decomposed into geometric and photometric components. Geometric parameters (position $\mathbf{p}$, scale $\mathbf{s}$, rotation $\mathbf{R}$) affect the projected 2D covariance $\Sigma_{2D}$ and mean $\boldsymbol{\mu}_{2D}$, which in turn affect $\alpha_k(\mathbf{x})$. Photometric parameters (color $\mathbf{c}_k$, opacity $\alpha_k$) affect the contribution directly.

Standard implementations compute these gradients using analytical derivatives of the 2D Gaussian kernel and the projection Jacobian. To optimize memory and throughput, implementations may use half-precision arithmetic and omit block-local reductions [S1, unofficial].

## Subtopics

### [ToF Gradient Computation for Gaussian Splatting](9733-tof-gradient-computation-for-gaussian-splatting.md)
Computes gradients for Time-of-Flight (ToF) signals, which involve non-linear accumulation of squared transmittance terms. It extends the standard RGB gradient path to handle quad pixel signals, requiring recursive accumulation of squared transmittance-weighted contributions. Choose this when training on ToF data.

### [Gradient-Weighted Feature Back-Projection](9769-gradient-weighted-feature-back-projection.md)
A training-free method to assign semantic features to Gaussians by back-projecting 2D features from training views weighted by the rendering gradient ($\alpha_k T_k$). It avoids iterative optimization of feature attributes. Choose this for semantic segmentation or [feature field](#12995-feature-fields.md) rendering without training a separate feature network.

### [SNS Backward Pass with Intermediate Variable Q](10040-sns-backward-pass-with-intermediate-variable-q.md)
Provides exact [analytical gradients](#7613-analytical-gradients.md) for Skew-Normal 2D density functions by introducing an intermediate variable $Q = ARS$ to decouple rotation and scale. It addresses the complex coupling in standard 3DGS gradients. Choose this when using Skew-Normal primitives for improved shape representation.

### [Specular-Aware Gradient Gating](13432-specular-aware-gradient-gating.md)
Suppresses specular artifacts in semi-transparent surfaces by modulating gradients for the transmission color component using a local variance-based gating factor. It applies a partial stop-gradient operation. Choose this for rendering glossy or semi-transparent materials where specular highlights cause training instability.

### [Deferred Back-propagation](13506-deferred-back-propagation.md)
Enables memory-efficient optimization for full-resolution image losses (e.g., VGG, NNFM) by decoupling loss computation from the differentiable render pass. It caches full-resolution gradients and re-renders small patches with auto-differentiation enabled. Choose this when using CNN-based losses that require full-resolution inputs and standard differentiable rendering runs out of GPU memory.

### Backward Pass in Half Precision
A gradient computation method using half-precision (FP16) arithmetic to optimize accuracy-throughput trade-off, omitting block-local reductions [S1, unofficial]. It calculates $\frac{\partial I}{\partial M_i}$ using Eqs. (3, 4, 5), $\frac{\partial M_i}{\partial u}$ using Eq. (2) and [bilinear interpolation](#858-bilinear-interpolation.md), and geometric derivatives from Eq. (1) [S1, unofficial]. The gradient of image $I$ w.r.t. primitive position $x_i$ is $\frac{\partial I(x,y)}{\partial x_i} = \frac{\partial I(x,y)}{\partial M_i(x,y)} \left( \frac{\partial M_i(x,y)}{\partial u} \frac{\partial u}{\partial x_i} + \frac{\partial M_i(x,y)}{\partial v} \frac{\partial v}{\partial x_i} \right)$, where $M_i$ is the primitive mask and $u,v$ are local coordinates [S1, unofficial]. It differs from standard implementations by using half precision and omitting block-local reductions to align with accuracy-throughput goals [S1, unofficial].

### Screenspace Points Gradient Buffer
A 2D tensor allocated per Gaussian to store gradients written by the CUDA backward pass, separating standard and absolute gradient channels [S2, unofficial]. It allocates a tensor of shape $(N, 4)$ with dtype matching xyz, sets `requires_grad=track_gradients`, and attempts to call `retain_grad()` to preserve gradients for intermediate computations, catching exceptions if unsupported [S2, unofficial]. The layout is $(N, 4)$ float32 tensor, where channels 0-1 store standard screen-space gradients and channels 2-3 store absolute gradients used by [ABSGS](#6127-absgs.md) and ImprovedGS [S2, unofficial]. Implementation involves `screenspace_points = torch.zeros((pc.get_xyz.shape[0], 4), dtype=pc.get_xyz.dtype, requires_grad=track_gradients, device=pc.get_xyz.device)` followed by a try/except block for `retain_grad()` [S2, unofficial]. A pitfall is that `retain_grad()` may raise an exception in older PyTorch versions or specific execution contexts, requiring a try/except block to prevent crashes [S2, unofficial].

## Background
The foundation of differentiable 3D [Gaussian Splatting](#946-gaussian-splatting.md) was established by Kerbl et al. in 2023 [G]. Subsequent work introduced optimizations for specific modalities and losses. DiffBMP [S1, unofficial] introduced [differentiable rendering with bitmap primitives](#13624-differentiable-bitmap-splatting.md) and half-precision backward passes. Improved-GS [S2, unofficial] introduced screenspace gradient buffers for advanced gradient handling. Other extensions like SNS [unofficial] and ToF-GS [unofficial] adapted the gradient path for specialized primitives and sensors.
